failure_policy: Separate explicit Root release is required for each resource, operation-clock and wholeSQL-clock group. Runtime is not authorized by plan generation.

All owned correctness/build/SQL/resource/cost processes must be terminal before clocks, and all other agents are quiet throughout each timing group. Do not stop unrelated existing services; report shared-host limits.
Same original drivers, SQL, oracle, fixture, persistence, allocator, timeouts and sample counts. No filters, retries, sample deletion, warmup discard, adaptive settings or selective reruns.
Preserve all raw values/errors/failed attempts/stdout/stderr/PIDs/exit flags. R15 shutdown failures stay visible and are not investigated or retried.

Resource or wholeSQL stage nonzero stops later stages/budgets. The three independent operation contexts may all be collected after a prior driver failure only if its actual owned process group and server context are absent; never call a failed label a pass.

Functional correctness must not regress and resource55 must complete before timing acceptance. No claim of universal improvement or automatic default promotion; report all35/36 p50 vs both old runs and old-run drift. Substantial regressions require evidence/review, not new samples.

default_promotion_review.functional_resource_status: Actual completed functional acceptance remains separate; resource55 passed. No expectation was weakened and no known failure is reclassified by this performance report.
default_promotion_review.reason: The new RETURNING correctness and window-query gains are valuable, but19/35 operation medians are higher than both old runs. In particular targeted rangeUPDATE is13.225/17.331percent slower with only−3.499percent old drift and processCPU medians540/570/540ms; targetedREINDEX is2.281/7.507percent slower. No universal acceleration or target-operation win is supported.
default_promotion_review.uncertainty: Six samples/operation in one sequential three-context pass do not isolate causality or establish statistical confidence. Shared-host/background work, processCPU jiffy granularity and old-run drift remain real; these caveats do not justify discarding slow samples or treating observed regressions as resolved.
default_promotion_review.next_allowed_reasoning: Keep the candidate/raws intact. Investigate default noncapture mutation/setup costs using existing source and public APIs before a new separately frozen candidate. Do not adapt/retry this completed matrix, infer correctness from speed, or start new experiments without Root release.

limits: One first call and three subsequent distinct statements per process, one process per generation/mode. Not a stable latency distribution or same-graph restart.
All wall/process/thread CPU preserved. Only default allocator clocks support the phase CPU comparison; counting-lane clocks are instrumented observations.
Cumulative C++ new/new[]/aligned requested counts/bytes are measured in the declared phase. They are not RSS, live allocation size, allocator usable size, all malloc traffic, or true peak.
The query/UPDATE predicates are the frozen typedexpr direct StorageEngine API controls. These observations do not prove the full Main benchmark UPDATE or REINDEX path improved.
Full setup DDL/heap insertion/commit cost is separately retained and is not assigned to parser or filter CPU.
Runtime input proof is read from saved before/after receipts; this static reducer does not repeat runtime or pretend current mutable product state was newly sampled.

data.unchanged_repeats: Each table: first public query plus three subsequent distinct public queries; first durable UPDATE plus three subsequent durable UPDATEs. Each invocation recreates statement-local filterRows cache; no retained graph/provider/frame.

limits: Process wall/process CPU/thread CPU are distinct absolute observations, not whole SQL/network latency.

Validation and fixture activity deliberately affect later cache state and are identical by method; no selective rerun or threshold.
N0/N1 can reveal new local-header/clone overhead; no assumed improvement.
Default durability, original mutation transaction and new-RID index maintenance remain.
Never run concurrently with Root performance windows; build/runtime require explicit Root release.

scope_summary: StorageEngine::prepareReturningDeclaration returns an owning QueryRowDescriptor and optional data-only physical origins. It reuses genuine catalog metadata/real target and FROM/USING/derived/nonrecursive CTE declarations; no executable partial query, cursor, planner or source-provider is returned.

A separate ReturningDeclarationBinder binds original RETURNING/output expressions and types; old Binder body is exact. INSERT VALUES/SELECT/default/conflict input, UPDATE SET/WHERE, DELETE predicates, MERGE ON/WHEN/action inputs, JOIN ON, grouping and final count/order expressions are not bound or evaluated for a declaration.

Actual occurrence/column ordinal identifies target and OLD/NEW origins through derived/CTE chains. Merged USING/set/computed outputs remain origin0; only already-bound identity Relabel casts preserve origin. View origin remains its own catalog relation. No output-name/type-text guessing.

A names-only RETURNING validator runs in an existing ordinary pre-Parse metadata helper and visits actual value ColumnRefs/stars only; EXTRACT grammar field is distinguished without treating date_part/qualified/quoted arguments as syntax. No function/type/CAST/value checking or effects is added by this namespace pass.

Private parseForReturningDeclaration admits original SELECT count AST syntax only for the two pure APIs. Dynamic ordinary SELECT count execution is not enabled. The TLS flag restores after success/error; public parse/parseForBinding bodies remain exact.

Network new declaration branch is limited to actual transition/image RETURNING shapes. Unknown parameter OIDs, missing metadata, unsupported structural declarations and paused top enum/enum-array/domain-enum return through complete old paths. Non-transition Describe and handleClient/Bind/portal/format2 ownership do not change.

Conditional explicit input casts/typed literals, expression SQL children, recursive declaration CTEs, function FROM sources and window declaration dependencies remain explicit unsupported ordinary coverage; no R106 input-analysis workaround or new deferral is claimed.

isolated_proposal.eligible: No expression/partial index, no virtual column, at least one auxiliary tree, total temporary trees including empty primary <=8
isolated_proposal.fallback: Entire old index-major body byte-exact; guard chooses it before creating a fast-path private tree. No failure-triggered retry.
isolated_proposal.per_tree_input: Each row/RID/key reaches the same original key helper and insert API in identical heap order; no string-based reclassification of types, collation, NULLs, uniqueness or OID.
isolated_proposal.ordinary_work_change: Two heap walks become one and raw row strings 2000->1000 for current two-tree fixture. Auxiliary maps remain 1000 for one secondary; with multiple ordinary auxiliary trees, share one owning map during genuine callback instead of rebuilding it per tree.
isolated_proposal.preserved: Original physical-index visibility flags false,true, metadata lock, original SQL key/null owners, old fallback, flush/close ordering, durable publish suffix, rollback recovery; no BPTree/PageAllocator/AtomicFile edits
isolated_proposal.resource_cost: Old BPTree::close closes buffer data/TDE descriptors and clears frames, but retains generationFd_ until destructor. New path opens <=8 pools together. At default 128x4096 per pool this is <=4MiB frame payload versus one active pool; DBMS_INDEX_BUFFER_FRAMES=4096 permits <=128MiB frame payload. These are payload-capacity bounds, not RSS/work_mem bounds; auxiliary nodes/allocator/tree metadata are extra. At most seven extra concurrently open data descriptors (and seven extra TDE descriptors when used) versus serial build; generation descriptors already accumulate in old path.
isolated_proposal.not_claimed: Not compiled, tested, benchmarked or accepted. Removing scans alone is not evidence of lower query latency; two-tree fixture only halves traversal/raw copy work, not tree insertion or fsync work.

reindex.later_bulk_build_alternative: PG/SQLite suggest sorted index tuple bulk loading could remove repeated root-to-leaf descent and splits. This requires a separate real sorted-key builder and resource/corruption/uniqueness/error tests; not included in current proposal and no PageAllocator exception/AtomicFile changes authorized.

primary_findings.finding: reindex_relation enumerates relation indexes and calls reindex_index for each. A single multi-index heap scan is our local guarded design, not a claim that PG universally does that.

B-tree build sorts index tuples then fills leaf/upper pages sequentially with explicit fill factors and bulk storage writes. Supports a separate future bulk-load design, not removing WAL/fsync from this engine.

ExecUpdateAct passes the real result slot and tuple identity into table_tuple_update; index update policy comes back from the table AM. Its omission conditions cannot be transplanted into this engine that changes RID mappings without corresponding heap-chain machinery.

Uses assignment-to-column maps and expression/predicate dependency checks to avoid unnecessary index work. Its own comments distinguish harmless conservative extra work from corrupting missed dependencies. This motivates exact dependency guards rather than skipping index maintenance on an unmodified key alone.
sqlite3RefillIndex fills a sorter, sorts generated index records and inserts in key order with seek-result reuse. Sorted rebuild is distinct from our narrower one-scan fanout.

PhysicalUpdate keeps reusable local update chunks, references existing input vectors and separately gathers RETURNING/old rows on demand. Demonstrates avoiding needless materialization while preserving transactional table.Update/Delete boundaries; it does not validate bypassing this engine's old/new ownership.

Verify REINDEX inside existing transaction, active inserted/updated/deleted versions, commit and rollback repairs, unique-key validation, failure before publication leaves live indexes complete and temporary files cleaned, original durable swap/recovery matrix unchanged.

Owned PID FD/path and allocator/process snapshots: bound simultaneous pool fanout and retained generation descriptors, after completion no new temporary/backup/swap marker leak. Do not probe deferred PageAllocator/AtomicFile failure investigations or shutdown.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validated operation benchmarks on a private cluster; never opens user data.

Mutation, transaction and maintenance latency includes durable completion.
Fixture setup, per-operation verification and cleanup are outside each timer.
SELECT fixtures and mutation results are checked against expected values.
All operations must complete without a protocol error; the read-only transaction
checks completion, and the sequence case checks its resulting currval.
"""
import argparse
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import random
import statistics
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import traceback

import benchmark_queries as query_bench
from postgres_protocol_test import read_message, read_until_ready, typed


class Operations:
    def __init__(self, client, pid, args, report):
        self.client, self.pid, self.args, self.report = client, pid, args, report
        self.cases = {}
        self.counts = Counter()

    def query(self, sql):
        return self.client.query(sql)

    def expect(self, sql, rows):
        actual = self.query(sql)
        assert Counter(map(tuple, actual)) == Counter(map(tuple, rows)), (sql, actual[:5], rows[:5])

    def add(self, name, action, verify, setup=lambda i: {}, cleanup=lambda c: None, units=1):
        self.cases[name] = (setup, action, verify, cleanup, units)

    def copy(self, sql, data=None):
        sock = self.client.sock
        sock.sendall(typed(b"Q", sql.encode() + b"\0"))
        kind, body = read_message(sock)
        assert kind == (b"H" if data is None else b"G"), (sql, kind, body)
        if data is not None:
            sock.sendall(typed(b"d", data) + typed(b"c"))
        messages = read_until_ready(sock)
        query_bench.checked_rows(messages)
        return b"".join(body for kind, body in messages if kind == b"d")

    def populate(self, table, rows):
        for start in range(1, rows + 1, 100):
            values = ",".join(f"({i},{i % 100},{i % 1000},'row-{i}')"
                              for i in range(start, min(rows + 1, start + 100)))
            self.query(f"INSERT INTO {table} VALUES {values}")

    def initialize(self):
        n, batch = self.args.rows, self.args.batch
        query_bench.load(self.client, n)
        self.client.prepare()
        specifications = query_bench.cases(n)
        for name, specification in specifications.items():
            self.add("select_" + name,
                     lambda c, name=name, specification=specification:
                         query_bench.execute_case(self.client, name, specification, c["i"]),
                     lambda c: None, setup=lambda i: {"i": i})
        schema = "(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,grp INTEGER,amount INTEGER,payload VARCHAR(64))"
        for table in ("op_insert", "op_bulk", "op_transaction", "op_rollback", "op_update", "op_indexed", "op_delete"):
            self.query("CREATE TABLE " + table + schema)
        for table in ("op_update", "op_indexed", "op_delete"):
            self.populate(table, n)
        self.query("CREATE INDEX op_secondary ON op_indexed(grp)")
        self.query("CREATE TABLE op_copy(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,payload TEXT)")
        self.query("CREATE TABLE op_toast(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,payload VARCHAR(12000))")
        self.query("CREATE SEQUENCE op_sequence")
        self.query("CHECKPOINT")

        def insert_setup(i, count=1):
            start = 1 + i * count
            return {"start": start, "count": count,
                    "values": ",".join(f"({k},{k % 100},{k % 1000},'row-{k}')"
                                        for k in range(start, start + count))}

        def inserted(table, context):
            start, count = context["start"], context["count"]
            self.expect(f"SELECT id,grp,amount,payload FROM {table} WHERE id BETWEEN {start} AND {start+count-1}",
                        [[str(k), str(k % 100), str(k % 1000), f"row-{k}"] for k in range(start, start + count)])

        self.add("insert_autocommit", lambda c: self.query("INSERT INTO op_insert VALUES " + c["values"]),
                 lambda c: inserted("op_insert", c), setup=insert_setup)
        self.add("insert_multi_values", lambda c: self.query("INSERT INTO op_bulk VALUES " + c["values"]),
                 lambda c: inserted("op_bulk", c), setup=lambda i: insert_setup(i, batch), units=batch)

        def transaction_insert(c):
            self.query("BEGIN")
            for k in range(c["start"], c["start"] + c["count"]):
                self.query(f"INSERT INTO op_transaction VALUES({k},{k%100},{k%1000},'row-{k}')")
            self.query("COMMIT")
        self.add("insert_explicit_transaction", transaction_insert,
                 lambda c: inserted("op_transaction", c), setup=lambda i: insert_setup(i, batch), units=batch)

        def update_setup(i):
            return {"id": i % n + 1, "value": 10000 + i}
        self.add("update_primary_key", lambda c: self.query(f"UPDATE op_update SET amount={c['value']} WHERE id={c['id']}"),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT amount FROM op_update WHERE id={c['id']}", [[str(c["value"])]]), setup=update_setup)
        self.add("update_secondary_index", lambda c: self.query(f"UPDATE op_indexed SET grp={c['value']} WHERE id={c['id']}"),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT id FROM op_indexed WHERE grp={c['value']}", [[str(c["id"])]]), setup=update_setup)
        self.add("update_cte_returning", lambda c: c.update(actual=self.query(
                     f"WITH marker AS (SELECT 1) UPDATE op_update SET amount={c['value']} WHERE id={c['id']} RETURNING id,amount")),
                 lambda c: self.check_returning_update(c), setup=update_setup)
        self.add("update_range", lambda c: self.query(f"UPDATE op_update SET amount={c['value']} WHERE id BETWEEN {c['start']} AND {c['start']+batch-1}"),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT id,amount FROM op_update WHERE id BETWEEN {c['start']} AND {c['start']+batch-1}",
                                       [[str(k), str(c["value"])] for k in range(c["start"], c["start"] + batch)]),
                 setup=lambda i: {"start": n // 2, "value": 20000 + i}, units=batch)
        self.add("delete_primary_key", lambda c: self.query(f"DELETE FROM op_delete WHERE id={c['id']}"),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT id FROM op_delete WHERE id={c['id']}", []), setup=lambda i: {"id": i + 1})
        self.add("delete_cte_returning", lambda c: c.update(actual=self.query(
                     f"WITH marker AS (SELECT 1) DELETE FROM op_delete WHERE id={c['id']} RETURNING id")),
                 lambda c: self.check_returning_delete(c), setup=lambda i: {"id": n-i})
        self.add("delete_range", lambda c: self.query(f"DELETE FROM op_delete WHERE id BETWEEN {c['start']} AND {c['start']+batch-1}"),
                 lambda c: self.expect("SELECT count(*) FROM op_delete", [[str(n - self.counts['delete_primary_key'] - self.counts['delete_range'] * batch - self.counts['delete_cte_returning'])]]),
                 setup=lambda i: {"start": n // 2 + i * batch}, units=batch)

        def transaction(c):
            for sql in c["statements"]:
                self.query(sql)
        self.add("transaction_read_commit", transaction, lambda c: None,
                 setup=lambda i: {"statements": ["BEGIN", "SELECT id FROM bench_rows WHERE id=1", "COMMIT"]})
        self.add("transaction_write_rollback", transaction,
                 lambda c: self.expect("SELECT count(*) FROM op_rollback", [["0"]]),
                 setup=lambda i: {"statements": ["BEGIN", f"INSERT INTO op_rollback VALUES({i+1},1,2,'rollback')", "ROLLBACK"]})
        self.add("transaction_savepoint", transaction,
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT amount FROM op_update WHERE id={n}", [["333"]]),
                 setup=lambda i: {"statements": ["BEGIN", f"UPDATE op_update SET amount=333 WHERE id={n}",
                     "SAVEPOINT op_sp", f"UPDATE op_update SET amount=444 WHERE id={n}",
                     "ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT op_sp", "RELEASE SAVEPOINT op_sp", "COMMIT"]})

        self.add("sequence_nextval", lambda c: c.update(actual=self.query("SELECT nextval('op_sequence')")),
                 lambda c: self.expect("SELECT currval('op_sequence')", [[str(c["i"] + 1)]]), setup=lambda i: {"i": i})
        self.add("copy_from", lambda c: self.copy("COPY op_copy FROM STDIN", c["data"]),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT id,payload FROM op_copy WHERE id BETWEEN {c['start']} AND {c['start']+batch-1}",
                                      [[str(k), f"row-{k}"] for k in range(c["start"], c["start"] + batch)]),
                 setup=lambda i: {"start": 1 + i * batch, "data": "".join(f"{k}\trow-{k}\n" for k in range(1+i*batch,1+(i+1)*batch)).encode()}, units=batch)
        self.add("copy_to", lambda c: c.update(actual=self.copy("COPY bench_rows TO STDOUT")),
                 lambda c: self.check_copy(c["actual"], n), units=n)
        payload = "0123456789abcdef" * 384
        self.add("toast_insert_6k", lambda c: self.query(f"INSERT INTO op_toast VALUES({c['id']},'{payload}')"),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT payload FROM op_toast WHERE id={c['id']}", [[payload]]), setup=lambda i: {"id": i + 1})

        def ddl_setup(i, stem, populated=False):
            table = f"{stem}_{i}"
            self.query(f"CREATE TABLE {table}(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)")
            if populated:
                self.query(f"INSERT INTO {table} VALUES " + ",".join(f"({k})" for k in range(1, self.args.ddl_rows + 1)))
            return {"table": table}
        self.add("ddl_create_table", lambda c: self.query(f"CREATE TABLE {c['table']}(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)"),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {c['table']}", [["0"]]),
                 setup=lambda i: {"table": f"op_create_{i}"}, cleanup=lambda c: self.query(f"DROP TABLE {c['table']}"))
        self.add("ddl_alter_add_column", lambda c: self.query(f"ALTER TABLE {c['table']} ADD COLUMN value INTEGER DEFAULT 5"),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT id,value FROM {c['table']}", [[str(k), "5"] for k in range(1, self.args.ddl_rows + 1)]),
                 setup=lambda i: ddl_setup(i, "op_alter", True), cleanup=lambda c: self.query(f"DROP TABLE {c['table']}"))
        self.add("ddl_truncate", lambda c: self.query(f"TRUNCATE TABLE {c['table']}"),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {c['table']}", [["0"]]),
                 setup=lambda i: ddl_setup(i, "op_truncate", True), cleanup=lambda c: self.query(f"DROP TABLE {c['table']}"))
        self.add("ddl_drop_table", lambda c: self.query(f"DROP TABLE {c['table']}"),
                 lambda c: self.expect(f"SELECT relname FROM pg_catalog.pg_class WHERE relname='{c['table']}'", []),
                 setup=lambda i: ddl_setup(i, "op_drop", True))
        for method in ("btree", "hash"):
            self.add("index_create_" + method,
                     lambda c, method=method: self.query(f"CREATE INDEX {c['index']} ON bench_rows USING {method}(grp)"),
                     lambda c: self.expect("SELECT id FROM bench_rows WHERE grp=42", [[str(k)] for k in range(1, n + 1) if k % 100 == 42]),
                     setup=lambda i, method=method: {"index": f"op_build_{method}_{i}"},
                     cleanup=lambda c: self.query(f"DROP INDEX {c['index']}"), units=n)
        self.add("maintenance_analyze", lambda c: self.query("ANALYZE bench_rows"),
                 lambda c: self.expect("SELECT count(*) FROM bench_rows", [[str(n)]]), units=n)
        self.add("maintenance_vacuum", lambda c: self.query("VACUUM op_delete"),
                 lambda c: self.expect("SELECT count(*) FROM op_delete", [[str(n-self.counts['delete_primary_key']-self.counts['delete_range']*batch-self.counts['delete_cte_returning'])]]))
        self.add("maintenance_reindex", lambda c: self.query("REINDEX TABLE op_indexed"),
                 lambda c: self.expect("SELECT count(*) FROM op_indexed", [[str(n)]]), units=n)
        self.add("maintenance_checkpoint", lambda c: self.query("CHECKPOINT"),
                 lambda c: self.expect("SELECT count(*) FROM bench_rows", [[str(n)]]))

    def check_copy(self, data, n):
        expected = [f"{k}\t{k%100}\t{k%1000}\trow-{k}" for k in range(1, n+1)]
        assert Counter(data.decode().splitlines()) == Counter(expected), "COPY output mismatch"

    def check_returning_update(self, context):
        assert context["actual"] == [[str(context["id"]), str(context["value"])]], context
        self.expect(f"SELECT amount FROM op_update WHERE id={context['id']}", [[str(context["value"])]])

    def check_returning_delete(self, context):
        assert context["actual"] == [[str(context["id"])]], context
        self.expect(f"SELECT id FROM op_delete WHERE id={context['id']}", [])

    def run(self, save):
        names = self.args.only or list(self.cases)
        assert all(name in self.cases for name in names), names
        for round_id in range(self.args.rounds):
            order = names[:]
            random.Random(3719 + round_id).shuffle(order)
            for name in order:
                setup, action, verify, cleanup, units = self.cases[name]
                samples = []
                for _ in range(self.args.samples):
                    index = self.counts[name]
                    context = setup(index)
                    before = query_bench.resources(self.pid)
                    start = time.perf_counter()
                    try:
                        action(context)
                    except BaseException:
                        self.report["failed_attempt"] = {"name": name, "round": round_id+1,
                            "sample": index+1, "elapsed_seconds": time.perf_counter()-start,
                            "before": before, "after": query_bench.resources(self.pid)}
                        save()
                        raise
                    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
                    after = query_bench.resources(self.pid)
                    self.counts[name] += 1
                    verify(context)
                    cleanup(context)
                    measured = query_bench.summarize([elapsed * 1000], elapsed, before, after)
                    measured.update(name=name, round=round_id+1, sample=index+1, units=units,
                                    units_per_second=units/elapsed)
                    self.report["measurements"].append(measured)
                    samples.append(elapsed * 1000)
                    save()
                print(f"OP round={round_id+1} {name} n={len(samples)} p50={statistics.median(samples):.3f}ms", flush=True)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--binary", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--rows", type=int, default=1000)
    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=50)
    parser.add_argument("--ddl-rows", type=int, default=5,
                        help="rows in each ALTER/TRUNCATE/DROP fixture, independent of DML batch size")
    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--samples", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--only", nargs="+")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if min(args.rows, args.batch, args.ddl_rows, args.rounds, args.samples) < 1 or args.rows < 100:
        parser.error("rows >= 100, positive batch/rounds/samples required")
    if args.batch * args.rounds * args.samples > args.rows // 2:
        parser.error("batch*rounds*samples must fit in half the fixture for distinct DELETE ranges")
    delete_samples = args.rounds * args.samples
    if (delete_samples >= args.rows // 2 or
            args.rows // 2 + args.batch * delete_samples - 1 >= args.rows - delete_samples + 1):
        parser.error("DELETE point, range and CTE fixtures must be disjoint; reduce batch/rounds/samples or increase rows")
    binary, output = args.binary.resolve(), args.output.resolve()
    if (output / "operations.json").exists():
        parser.error("output already contains operations.json")
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="data-operations-", dir=output))
    (data / "info").mkdir(); (data / "info/tlist.lst").touch()
    query_bench.write_auth_catalog(str(data), "alice", "secret")
    (data / "pg_hba.conf").write_text("host all alice 127.0.0.1/32 scram-sha-256\n")
    report = {"created_utc": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), "binary": str(binary),
              "binary_sha256": hashlib.sha256(binary.read_bytes()).hexdigest(), "data_directory": str(data),
              "arguments": {k: str(v) if isinstance(v, Path) else v for k,v in vars(args).items()},
              "settings": "server defaults, persistence unchanged; loopback reused connection; no TLS",
              "measurement": "setup, mutation verification and cleanup excluded; query validation included; all successful samples verified; mutation and commit included",
              "measurements": [], "complete": False}
    def save():
        (output / "operations.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    save()
    try:
        with query_bench.server(binary, data, output / "server.log") as (client, pid, port):
            operations = Operations(client, pid, args, report)
            print("FIXTURE_LOADING", flush=True)
            operations.initialize()
            report["available_cases"] = list(operations.cases)
            print("FIXTURE_READY", len(operations.cases), "cases", flush=True)
            operations.run(save)
        report["complete"] = True
        save()
        print("OPERATIONS_COMPLETE all measured results validated", flush=True)
    except BaseException as error:
        report["failure"] = repr(error)
        (output / "failure.txt").write_text(traceback.format_exc())
        save()
        raise


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure validated SQL queries against a private, disposable DBMS cluster.

Example:
  python3 scripts/benchmark_queries.py --binary /absolute/path/dbms_main \
      --output build/query-benchmark --rows 1000 10000 --profile

The binary is never rebuilt by this driver. Every run creates its own data
directory, keeps default server settings, and reports client round-trip latency
separately from server CPU and /proc I/O counters. Connection authentication,
fixture loading, warmups and EXPLAIN are outside measured intervals. Profiles
run separately, so their instrumentation does not contaminate baseline times.
"""

import argparse
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
from pathlib import Path
import platform
import random
import shutil
import signal
import socket
import statistics
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time


REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "tests"))
from postgres_protocol_test import (data_row_values, diagnostic_fields,
                                    read_until_ready, simple_query, startup,
                                    typed, write_auth_catalog)


def checked_rows(messages):
    for kind, body in messages:
        if kind == b"E":
            fields = diagnostic_fields(body)
            raise RuntimeError({k.decode(): v.decode(errors="replace")
                                for k, v in fields.items()})
    if not messages or messages[-1][0] != b"Z":
        raise RuntimeError("query did not complete with ReadyForQuery")
    return [[None if cell is None else cell.decode("utf-8") for cell in row]
            for row in data_row_values(messages)]


class Client:
    def __init__(self, port):
        self.sock = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=60)
        self.sock.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1)
        startup(self.sock, "alice", "info", validate_dbms_status=False,
                application_name="query-performance-benchmark")

    def query(self, sql):
        return checked_rows(simple_query(self.sock, sql))

    def prepare(self):
        sql = "SELECT id,grp,amount,payload FROM bench_rows WHERE id=$1"
        body = b"bench_pk\0" + sql.encode() + b"\0" + struct.pack("!HI", 1, 23)
        self.sock.sendall(typed(b"P", body) + typed(b"S"))
        messages = read_until_ready(self.sock)
        checked_rows(messages)
        if not any(kind == b"1" for kind, _ in messages):
            raise RuntimeError("missing ParseComplete")

    def prepared_point(self, key):
        body = (b"\0bench_pk\0" + struct.pack("!HHH", 1, 1, 1)
                + struct.pack("!iiH", 4, key, 0))
        self.sock.sendall(typed(b"B", body) + typed(b"D", b"P\0")
                          + typed(b"E", b"\0" + struct.pack("!I", 0))
                          + typed(b"S"))
        return checked_rows(read_until_ready(self.sock))

    def close(self):
        try:
            self.sock.sendall(typed(b"X"))
        except OSError:
            pass
        self.sock.close()


def target_pid(process, binary):
    pending = [process.pid]
    while pending:
        pid = pending.pop()
        try:
            command = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline").read_bytes().split(b"\0")
            if command[0] == str(binary).encode() and b"--server" in command:
                return pid
            children = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/task/{pid}/children").read_text()
            pending.extend(map(int, children.split()))
        except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError):
            pass
    raise RuntimeError("cannot identify the benchmark server process")


@contextmanager
def server(binary, data, log_path, experiment=None, command_prefix=()):
    probe = socket.socket()
    probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    port = probe.getsockname()[1]
    probe.close()
    command = [str(binary), "--data-dir", str(data), "--server", str(port),
               "--insecure"]
    if experiment:
        # Clock sampling avoids the collector's I/O interposition hooks.
        # Some gprofng/glibc combinations cannot trace llseek/OFD locking;
        # trace system calls in a separate strace run when needed.
        command = ["gprofng", "collect", "app", "-p", "1",
                   "-o", str(experiment)] + command
    command = list(command_prefix) + command
    environment = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()
                   if not k.startswith("DBMS_")}
    environment["DBMS_DATA_DIR"] = str(data)
    with log_path.open("w") as log:
        process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=data, env=environment,
                                   stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                                   start_new_session=True)
        client = None
        pid = None
        try:
            deadline = time.monotonic() + 30
            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                if process.poll() is not None:
                    raise RuntimeError("server exited at startup: "
                                       + log_path.read_text()[-3000:])
                try:
                    client = Client(port)
                    break
                except (ConnectionRefusedError, ConnectionResetError):
                    time.sleep(0.05)
            if client is None:
                raise RuntimeError("server startup deadline exceeded")
            pid = target_pid(process, binary)
            yield client, pid, port
        finally:
            if client:
                client.close()
            if process.poll() is None:
                if pid:
                    try:
                        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGTERM)
                    except ProcessLookupError:
                        pass
                else:
                    os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
                try:
                    process.wait(timeout=30)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                    process.wait()
                    raise RuntimeError("benchmark server required forced shutdown")
            if process.returncode:
                raise RuntimeError(f"server exited with {process.returncode}: "
                                   + log_path.read_text()[-2000:])


def resources(pid):
    fields = Path(f"/proc/{pid}/stat").read_text().rsplit(")", 1)[1].split()
    hz = os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK")
    result = {"user_seconds": int(fields[11]) / hz,
              "system_seconds": int(fields[12]) / hz}
    for line in Path(f"/proc/{pid}/io").read_text().splitlines():
        name, value = line.split(":")
        result[name] = int(value)
    for line in Path(f"/proc/{pid}/status").read_text().splitlines():
        if line.startswith(("VmRSS:", "VmHWM:", "Threads:")):
            name, value, *_ = line.split()
            result[name.rstrip(":")] = int(value)
    return result


def summarize(latencies, elapsed, before, after):
    ordered = sorted(latencies)
    count = len(ordered)
    if not count:
        raise RuntimeError("empty measurement")
    delta = {key: after[key] - before[key] for key in before
             if key not in {"VmRSS", "VmHWM", "Threads"}}
    cpu = delta["user_seconds"] + delta["system_seconds"]
    return {"queries": count, "errors": 0, "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
            "qps": count / elapsed, "mean_ms": statistics.mean(ordered),
            "p50_ms": statistics.median(ordered),
            "p95_ms": ordered[math.ceil(count * 0.95) - 1],
            "max_ms": ordered[-1], "server_cpu_ms_per_query": cpu * 1000 / count,
            "server_cpu_cores": cpu / elapsed, "server_io_delta": delta,
            "server_rss_kib": after["VmRSS"], "latencies_ms": latencies}


def cases(size):
    def key(i):
        return 1 + ((i * 7919 + size // 2) % size)

    def row(k):
        return [str(k), str(k % 100), str(k % 1000), f"row-{k}"]

    low, high = max(1, size // 2), min(size, size // 2 + 99)
    totals = [[str(group), str(sum(i % 100 == group for i in range(1, size + 1))),
               str(sum(i % 1000 for i in range(1, size + 1) if i % 100 == group))]
              for group in range(100)]
    top = [[str(i), str(i % 1000)] for i in
           sorted(range(1, size + 1), key=lambda i: (-(i % 1000), i))[:20]]
    return {

                      + str(key(i)), lambda i: [row(key(i))]),
        "pk_prepared": (lambda i: key(i), lambda i: [row(key(i))]),
        "unindexed_lookup": (lambda i: "SELECT id,grp,amount,payload FROM bench_rows WHERE payload='row-"

                       lambda i: top),
        "join_count": (lambda i: "SELECT count(*) FROM bench_rows r JOIN bench_groups g ON r.grp=g.id",

def execute_case(client, name, specification, iteration):
    sql, expected = specification
    actual = (client.prepared_point(sql(iteration)) if name == "pk_prepared"
              else client.query(sql(iteration)))
    wanted = expected(iteration)
    if actual != wanted:
        raise AssertionError((name, sql(iteration), "actual", actual[:5],
                              "expected", wanted[:5], "counts", len(actual), len(wanted)))


def measure(client, pid, name, specification, seconds, maximum):
    # Warm the statement, relation buffers and connection before measuring.
    for i in range(2):
        execute_case(client, name, specification, i)
    before = resources(pid)
    begin = time.perf_counter()
    latencies = []
    while len(latencies) < maximum:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        execute_case(client, name, specification, len(latencies))
        latencies.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000)
        if len(latencies) >= 3 and time.perf_counter() - begin >= seconds:
            break
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - begin
    return summarize(latencies, elapsed, before, resources(pid))


def load(client, size):
    client.query("CREATE TABLE bench_rows(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,grp INTEGER,amount INTEGER,payload VARCHAR(64))")
    client.query("CREATE TABLE bench_groups(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,label VARCHAR(32))")
    client.query("BEGIN")
    for start in range(1, size + 1, 200):
        values = ",".join(f"({i},{i % 100},{i % 1000},'row-{i}')"
                          for i in range(start, min(size + 1, start + 200)))
        client.query("INSERT INTO bench_rows VALUES " + values)
    client.query("INSERT INTO bench_groups VALUES " + ",".join(
        f"({i},'group-{i}')" for i in range(100)))
    client.query("COMMIT")
    client.query("ANALYZE bench_rows")
    client.query("ANALYZE bench_groups")
    if client.query("SELECT count(*) FROM bench_rows") != [[str(size)]]:
        raise AssertionError("fixture row count mismatch")
    client.query("CHECKPOINT")


def concurrency(pid, port, size, clients, seconds):
    ready = threading.Barrier(clients + 1)
    deadline = [None]
    spec = cases(size)["pk_lookup"]

    def worker(worker_id):
        client = Client(port)
        try:
            execute_case(client, "pk_lookup", spec, worker_id)
            ready.wait(timeout=70)
            values = []
            while time.perf_counter() < deadline[0]:
                start = time.perf_counter()
                execute_case(client, "pk_lookup", spec,
                             len(values) * clients + worker_id)
                values.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000)
            return values
        finally:
            client.close()

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=clients) as pool:
        futures = [pool.submit(worker, i) for i in range(clients)]
        # Wait for authentication/warmup before taking the resource baseline.
        while ready.n_waiting != clients:
            if any(f.done() and f.exception() for f in futures):
                raise next(f.exception() for f in futures if f.done() and f.exception())
            time.sleep(0.01)
        before = resources(pid)
        begin = time.perf_counter()
        deadline[0] = begin + seconds
        ready.wait(timeout=70)
        latencies = [v for f in futures for v in f.result()]
        result = summarize(latencies, time.perf_counter() - begin,
                           before, resources(pid))
        result["clients"] = clients
        return result

                        help="minimum measured interval for each concurrency block")
    parser.add_argument("--profile", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--profile-from", type=Path,
                        help="profile a prior run's private cluster without repeating its baseline")
    parser.add_argument("--fixture-from", type=Path,
                        help="copy a prior benchmark's private fixtures for a controlled comparison")
    parser.add_argument("--profile-seconds", type=float, default=8)
    parser.add_argument("--profile-cases", nargs="+",
                        default=["pk_lookup", "group_aggregate", "sort_limit"])
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if (min(args.rows) < 100 or args.rounds < 1 or args.seconds <= 0
            or args.concurrency_seconds <= 0 or args.profile_seconds <= 0
            or args.max_queries < 3):
        parser.error("rows >= 100, rounds >= 1, seconds > 0 and max-queries >= 3 required")
    binary, output = args.binary.resolve(), args.output.resolve()
    if not binary.is_file():

              "binary": str(binary), "binary_sha256": hashlib.sha256(binary.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
              "platform": platform.platform(), "python": sys.version,

            data = Path(directory).resolve()

                    or not data.name.startswith(f"data-{size}-")

        report["baseline_source_failure"] = prior.get("failure")
        report["baseline_source_case_blocks"] = len(prior["cases"])
        report["baseline_source_concurrency_blocks"] = len(prior["concurrency"])

        print(text, flush=True)

                    if name != "pk_prepared":
                        plans[name] = client.query("EXPLAIN " + sql(0))
                (output / f"plans-{size}.json").write_text(json.dumps(plans, indent=2))
                progress(f"LOADED rows={size}")
                for round_id in range(args.rounds):
                    names = list(specifications)
                    random.Random(1729 + round_id).shuffle(names)
                    for name in names:
                        measured = measure(client, pid, name, specifications[name],
                                           args.seconds, args.max_queries)

                                         "example_input": specifications[name][0](0)})
                        report["cases"].append(measured)
                        progress(f"CASE rows={size} round={round_id + 1} {name} "
                                 f"n={measured['queries']} p50={measured['p50_ms']:.3f}ms "
                                 f"p95={measured['p95_ms']:.3f}ms qps={measured['qps']:.1f}")
                if size == max(args.rows):
                    for clients in (1, 4):
                        for round_id in range(args.rounds):
                            measured = concurrency(pid, port, size, clients,
                                                   args.concurrency_seconds)
                            measured.update({"round": round_id + 1, "rows": size, "name": "pk_lookup"})
                            report["concurrency"].append(measured)
                            progress(f"CONCURRENCY clients={clients} round={round_id + 1} "
                                     f"n={measured['queries']} p50={measured['p50_ms']:.3f}ms "
                                     f"p95={measured['p95_ms']:.3f}ms qps={measured['qps']:.1f}")

            size = max(args.rows)
            data = Path(report["data_directories"][str(size)])
            specifications = cases(size)
            for name in args.profile_cases:
                if name not in specifications:
                    raise ValueError("unknown profile case " + name)
                experiment = output / f"profile-{name}.er"
                with server(binary, data, output / f"profile-{name}.log", experiment) as (client, pid, port):
                    client.prepare()
                    measured = measure(client, pid, name, specifications[name],
                                       args.profile_seconds, 100000)
                measured.update({"name": name, "rows": size, "experiment": str(experiment),
                                 "instrumented": True})
                report["profiles"].append(measured)
                command = ["gprofng", "display", "text", "-limit", "50", "-header", "-functions", str(experiment)]
                with (output / f"profile-{name}-functions.txt").open("w") as stream:
                    subprocess.run(command, stdout=stream, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, check=True, timeout=90)
                progress(f"PROFILE_COMPLETE {name} queries={measured['queries']}")
        report["complete"] = True
        progress("BENCHMARK_COMPLETE all measured SQL results validated; errors=0")
    except BaseException as error:
        report["complete"] = False
        report["failure"] = repr(error)
        save()
        raise

    main()

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import signal
import socket
import threading
import time

from runtime_observe_window_sql import files, owner, query, row_digest, sha, specifications, tree


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--binary", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--fixture", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    binary, fixture, output = args.binary.resolve(), args.fixture.resolve(), args.output.resolve()
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    data = output / "data"; original = tree(fixture); shutil.copytree(fixture, data)
    spec = specifications()[0]; wanted = spec["expected"]
    response = {}; observed = []; identity = None; pid = None; stopped = killed = False
    result = {"complete": False, "binary_sha256": sha(binary), "driver_sha256": sha(__file__),
              "resource_driver_sha256": sha(Path(__file__).with_name("runtime_observe_window_sql.py")),
              "fixture_hashes": original, "sql": spec["sql"], "branches": spec["branches"],
              "scope": "Owned read-only ordinary final TypedSort after a physical window SIGKILL with a verified live anonymous spool; "
                       "same private data directory reopen validates1000 committed rows/4000cells. "
                       "Window partitions/stage sorting remain unbounded and create no window spool. No arbitrary mutation/crash-recovery or OPT10 completion claim."}
    def owned_signal(sig):
        current = owner(pid, binary, data)
        assert identity is not None and current["start_ticks"] == identity["start_ticks"]
        os.kill(pid, sig)
    try:
        try:
            with query.server(binary, data, output / "before.log") as (client, pid, _):
                client.sock.settimeout(15); identity = owner(pid, binary, data); result["owner"] = identity
                assert client.query("SET work_mem='64kB'") == []
                assert client.query("SHOW work_mem") == [["64kB"]]
                def request():
                    try:
                        response["rows"] = client.query(spec["sql"])
                    except BaseException as error:
                        response["error"] = repr(error)
                worker = threading.Thread(target=request); worker.start(); deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
                try:
                    while worker.is_alive() and time.monotonic() < deadline:
                        if files(pid) and all(target.endswith(" (deleted)") for target in files(pid).values()):
                            owned_signal(signal.SIGSTOP); stopped = True; stop_deadline = time.monotonic() + 1
                            stop_confirmed = False
                            while time.monotonic() < stop_deadline:
                                if Path(f"/proc/{pid}/status").read_text().split("State:", 1)[1].lstrip().startswith("T"):
                                    stop_confirmed = True
                                    break
                                time.sleep(.0001)
                            assert stop_confirmed, "owned process did not enter stopped state"
                            current = files(pid)
                            if current:
                                observed.append(current); break
                            owned_signal(signal.SIGCONT); stopped = False
                        time.sleep(.0001)
                    assert observed, "No actual ordinary final TypedSort spool captured; response=" + repr(
                        {key: len(value) if key == "rows" else value for key, value in response.items()})
                    assert len(observed[0]) <= 2 and all(
                        target.startswith(str(data / ".dbms-sort-")) and "(deleted)" in target
                        for target in observed[0].values())
                    assert not list(data.glob(".dbms-sort-*"))
                    owned_signal(signal.SIGKILL); stopped = False; killed = True
                    worker.join(timeout=5); assert not worker.is_alive()
                    assert "error" in response and "rows" not in response
                finally:
                    if stopped:
                        owned_signal(signal.SIGCONT); stopped = False
                    if worker.is_alive():
                        try:
                            client.sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
                        except OSError:
                            pass
                        worker.join(timeout=5)
                    assert not worker.is_alive(), "private crash worker did not stop"
        except RuntimeError as error:
            assert killed and observed and "server exited with -9:" in str(error), repr(error)
            result["expected_server_exit"] = str(error).split(":", 1)[0]
        assert killed and pid is not None and not Path(f"/proc/{pid}").exists()
        assert not list(data.glob(".dbms-sort-*"))
        result["observed_live_sort_descriptors"] = observed
        result["connection_after_kill"] = response
        with query.server(binary, data, output / "reopen.log") as (client, reopened_pid, _):
            client.sock.settimeout(15); result["reopened_owner"] = owner(reopened_pid, binary, data)
            actual = client.query("SELECT id,grp,amount,payload FROM bench_rows ORDER BY id")
            expected_all = [[str(i), str(i % 100), str(i % 1000), "row-" + str(i)] for i in range(1, 1001)]
            assert actual == expected_all
            assert client.query("SET work_mem='64kB'") == []
            assert client.query("SHOW work_mem") == [["64kB"]]
            sorted_rows = client.query(spec["sql"]); assert sorted_rows == wanted
            assert not files(reopened_pid) and not list(data.glob(".dbms-sort-*"))
            result.update({"reopened_exact_rows": len(actual), "reopened_exact_cells": sum(map(len, actual)),
                           "reopened_cells_sha256": row_digest(actual), "sorted_rows_revalidated": len(sorted_rows),
                           "sorted_values_sha256": row_digest(sorted_rows)})
        result["source_fixture_unchanged"] = tree(fixture) == original
        assert result["source_fixture_unchanged"]; result["complete"] = True
    except BaseException as error:
        result["error"] = repr(error); raise
    finally:
        if stopped and pid is not None and Path(f"/proc/{pid}").exists():
            owned_signal(signal.SIGCONT)
        (output / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
